questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to Asia and have always dreamed of going to Japan. I picked because of the country and city, not the university and academics. Waseda University was the only university in Japan that had courses relevant for my studies at home.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was amazing, I loved being on exchange in Tokyo. The culture, food and city in general exceeded my expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not easy. Waseda University's website can be quite a jungle. Moreover, many documents were needed to go on exchange to Japan and except spending a lot of time preparing these.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get much help. I did however live with other exchange students  that went to the same university as me, so we were able to help each other a lot. The school also sent out a list of things we had to do upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It is an experience going to the Japanese city office, which is mandatory upon arrival as many don't speak english.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got my second choice and found housing through Waseda University. I lived off campus at a dorm called Rikkokai. It was super cheap and had a great location. However, it was very small and a bit dirty.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is no problem living off campus in Tokyo as public transportation is super good and it's easy to get around.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration was easy to figure out and is over three rounds. Pick more courses than you need the first time as it is not sure that you get all your picks. You can drop courses in the second and third round. I got all the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Waseda University sent out multiple emails regarding course registration. They had all information needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful as i got all the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for more courses than you need in the first round. Take the course "Japanese for zero beginners".

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to take a lot of courses (I had 9) and the system is very different than in Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is easier than in Denmark and going to Waseda University is a bit like going to high school. You have multiple (4-5) weekly assignments. The exams are easy and in some courses I didn't have any exams.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Many assingments, a few presentations, more home work than in Copenhagen. I read way less and didn't prepare for exams much.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Immunology, 1 credit=2 ECTS-points
Introduction to Computational Physics, 2 credits=4 ECTS-points
Current Topics in Biosciences, 2 credits=4 ECTS-points
Molecular Cell Biology A, 2 credits=4 ECTS-points
Research Design and Analysis, 2 credits=4 ECTS-points
Japanese for 'Zero' Beginners, 2 credits=4 ECTS-points
Budo, 1 credit = 2 ECTS-points
History of pre-Modern Japan, 2 credits = 4 ECTS-points
History of Modern Japan, 2 credits = 4 ECTS-points

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Japanese for 'Zero' Beginners is a great course if you want to learn a bit Japanese and is a course for only exchange students. Except a big workload and weekly quizzes.

History of pre-Modern Japan and History of Modern Japan are great courses where you go to museums and other trips every week. Afterwards, there is a weekly assignment. I really enjoyed these courses. 

Budo is a super fun course and nothing like going to university. Everyone pass the class and the teachers are super nice. 

Don't take research and design, nor Introduction to Computational Physics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There is a mandatory national insurance in Japan for about 1700 yen (75 kr). every month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating put is super cheap and really good. I ate out around once a day. Fruit is super expensive in the supermarket and every fruit is huge.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Waseda University have many many clubs but it is very hard to get accepted into. I wrote to four different and didn't hear back from any of them. You cannot join a sportsteam either.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club if you can.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on trips almost every weekend with the friends i made at my dorm. You have to go to the Mount Fuji area (lake Kawaguchi). Other recommendations outside Tokyo is Nikko, Kansai-area (Osaka, Kyoto, Nara) and mountains as Mount Takao and Mount Otake. Tokyo is amazing and there is so much to see. Go explore all the big areas as Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ikebukuro, Akihabara, Ginza and Ueno.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it hard even though there are big cultural differences. You quickly get used to the differences and learn how to act. The Japanese people are super polite, respectful and nice. They also queue up.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take courses that are not exclusive for exchange students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier. Nonetheless, Google Image translate is a lifesaver and help you a lot.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Japanese people are so respectful, helpful and nice. I love how quite the they are in public transport.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It a lot of work to go to Tokyo as you have to take a language test, take physical pictures that have to be sent to Japan, prepare 15+ documents and go to the embassy multiple times prior. It is however totally worth it!
The food and culture is amazing.
Live in a dorm. I got almost all my friends from the dorm i stayed at.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing Tokyo and Japan and meeting friends from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The beginning, where you are far from everything, don't know anyone and can't speak the language.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Learning to speak and read a bit Japanese is very helpful.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
